target_statement: Solve the complete six nilpotent affine-Hamiltonian pair sources for unimodular quadratic symplectic Poisson tensors, and test whether every primitive first-jet evaluation is noninjective.
implication_to_classification: For a highest part with a nonzero linear Casimir, its full Hamiltonian field is affine and nowhere zero. Semisimple and constant affine Hamiltonians force a constant translation symmetry, hence a kernel of the first jet. The six nilpotent pairs are the exact remaining types. If all six sources have identically vanishing4x4 evaluation minors or are rank4-empty, the entire linear-Casimir highest-part branch has proper primitive-beta image.
coefficient_ring: QQ and all free parameters of each exact affine linear source, no coefficient point evaluation
hypotheses: For each canonical nowhere-zero affine V and nonzero linear function ell with V(ell)=0, fix P#dell=V and retain all45 coefficients of the three other brackets. Impose divP=0 and all positive-degree coefficients of PfP=0. These are affine linear equations; in dimension4 divP=0 plus constantPf is equivalent to Jacobi.
inverted_elements: Only PfP!=0 for the rank4 source; no source parameter is divided out in solving the full linear system
complements: The semisimple and constant affine-Hamiltonian types have a separate translation-symmetry proof
Highest parts without a nonzero linear Casimir remain open
If a source has injective evaluation, no non-dominance conclusion is drawn from its dimension alone
success_certificate: Every full45-variable affine solution and dimension; universal Hamiltonian identity, divergence and Jacobi; constantPf; the full6x4 first-jet evaluation matrix and all15 maximal minors. No sampled points or partial source equations.
independent_check: A separate reader verifies all affine pair orbits and the no-zero implication. An independent coefficient implementation checks the linear sources and the small maximal-minor identities before using the support exclusion.
negative_result_next_step: If injective sources remain, keep their complete parameterizations and investigate a structural invariant or image-dimension bound. Do not repeat coefficient samples or discard those sources.
